title.narrative: Lao PDR Priority Skills for Growth

description.narrative: The development objective of Priority Skills for Growth Project for Lao People's Democratic Republic is to enhance access, quality and relevance of skills development and employment services for youth and other vulnerable groups in priority sectors, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it. This project has four components. The first component, Improving the quality and relevance of the TVET system, has the following sub-comp[onents: System-level reform; and : Institution-level reform. The second component, Enhancing job matching and youth employability, has the following sub-components: Strengthening the service delivery capacity of employment services; and Skills development and employment generation support for priority groups. The third component, Better governance, project management, and M&E support, has the following sub-components: Improving system performance; and Project Management and M&E. The fourth component, Contingent Emergency Response, would allow rapid reallocation of credits proceeds to respond to unanticipated eligible crises or emergencies.

To enhance access, quality and relevance of skills development and employment services for youth and other vulnerable groups in priority sectors, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

condition.narrative: Annual Work Plans and BudgetsFinancing Agreement Schedule 2, Section I Para CThe Recipient, through MoES and MoLSW, shall: (a)prepare, not later than December 1 of each year, an annual work plan and budget (“Annual Work Plans and Budget”) for theirRespective Parts of the Project for the following fiscal year of the Recipient, in a manner and substance satisfactory to theAssociation, covering the activities and expenditures proposed for the subsequent year of Project implementation, and the source(s)of financing of such activities and expenditures; which plan and budget shall be of such scope and detail as the Association shallhave reasonably requested, except for the Annual Work Plans and Budget for the first fiscal year of the Recipient which shall befurnished to the Association prior to the commencement of the relevant activities under the Project; and (b) thereafter implementtheir Respective Parts of the Project during the relevant fiscal year of the Recipient in accordance with such plan and budget asagreed with the Association.

Contingent Emergency Response ComponentFinancing Agreement Schedule 2, Section I Para E1. In order to ensure the properimplementation of contingent emergency response activities under Part 4 of the Project (“Contingent Emergency Response Part”), theRecipient shall ensure that:(a) the CERC Manual is prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to the Association, whichshall set forth detailed implementation arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part, including: (i) any structures orinstitutional arrangements for coordinating and implementing the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (ii) specific activities whichmay be included in the Contingent Emergency Response Part, Eligible Expenditures required therefor (“Emergency Expenditures”), andany procedures for such inclusion; (iii) financial management arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (iv)procurement methods and procedures for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (v) documentation required for withdrawals ofFinancing amounts to finance Emergency Expenditures; (vi) a description of the environmental and social assessment and managementarrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; and (vii) a template Emergency Action Plan; (b) the Emergency Action Planis prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to the Association; (c) the Emergency Response Part is carried out inaccordance with the CERC Manual and the Emergency Action Plan; provided, however, that in the event of any inconsistency betweenthe provisions of the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan and this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail;and (d) neither the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan is amended, suspended, abrogated, repealed or waived without the priorwritten approval by the Association.2. The Recipient shall ensure that the structures and arrangements referred to in the CERCManual are maintained throughout the implementation of the Contingent Emergency Response Part, with adequate staff and resourcessatisfactory to Association.3. The Recipient shall ensure that:(a) the environmental and social instruments required for theContingent Emergency Response Part are prepared, disclosed and adopted in accordance with the CERC Manual and the ESCP, and in formand substance acceptable to the Association; and(b) the Contingent Emergency Response Part is carried out in accordance with theenvironmental and social instruments in a manner acceptable to the Association.4. The activities under the Contingency EmergencyResponse Part shall be undertaken only after an Eligible Crisis or Emergency has occurred.

Environmental and Social StandardsFinancing Agreement Schedule 2, Section I Para DThe Recipient, through MoES and MoLSW, shallensure that their Respective Parts of the Project are carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in amanner acceptable to the Association. Without limitation upon paragraph 1 above, the Recipient, through MoES and MoLSW, shallensure that their Respective Parts of the Project are implemented in accordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan(“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient, through MoES and MoLSW, shall ensure that:(a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligence and efficiency, as provided in theESCP;(b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP;(c) policies and procedures are maintained,and qualified and experienced staff in adequate numbers are retained to implement the ESCP, as provided in the ESCP; and(d) theESCP, or any provision thereof, is not amended, repealed, suspended or waived, except as the Association shall otherwise agree inwriting, as specified in the ESCP, and ensure that the revised ESCP is disclosed promptly thereafter.

Institutional ArrangementsFinancing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I Para AThe Recipient shall, through MoES and MoLSW,maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, Project implementation structures at the national andsub-national levels, all with composition, functions, staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association and set out in theProject Implementation Manual (“PIM”). The Recipient shall, through MoES and MoLSW, monitor Project progress against the agreedperformance indicators and produce periodic progress reports.Without limitation to foregoing, the Recipient, through MoES andMoLSW, shall: (a)maintain a Project Steering Committee (“PSC”), an inter-ministerial body which shall be responsible, inter alia,for: providing policy and strategy guidance and making key decision on complex implementation issues in line with the PIM; andapproving the annual plans, budgets, audits and annual technical reports before submission to the Association for approval;(b) maintain Project Implementation Teams within the two Ministries, which shall be responsible, inter alia, for: implementingproject activities and monitor progress against the agreed performance indicators and produce periodic progress reports; and (c)maintain a Project Coordination Unit (“PCU”), which shall be responsible, inter alia, for: providing coordination for the projectand liaise with the Association and other relevant agencies.

Project Implementation ManualFinancing Agreement Schedule 2, Section I Para BThe Recipient, through MoES and MoLSW, shall ensurethat their Respective Parts of the Project are carried out in accordance with the arrangements and procedures set out in theProject Implementation Manual (“PIM”), which shall include, inter alia, (i) detailed operational guidelines, monitoring andreporting mechanisms, fiduciary procedures and requirements, and project documentation; and (ii) eligibility criteria ofbeneficiaries receiving Scholarships and Stipends, methodology for calculating the amount of Scholarships and Stipends, and relateddisbursement, financial management, monitoring and evaluation procedures.
